title: Rational affine-space parameters give isomorphic line-module fibres
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume $X$ is normal, meaning that each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $n\geq0$, let $U$ be an open subscheme of $\mathbf A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $p,q\in U(k)$. For every invertible module $\mathcal N$ on $X\times_kU$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-sc-invertible-module], there is an isomorphism $i_p^*\mathcal N\simeq i_q^*\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, where $i_r(x)=(x,r)$ and pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_kU$ and $f=\operatorname{pr}_X$. Since every ideal of a field is zero or the unit ideal, $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian. The finite-type hypothesis on $X$ and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] imply that $X$ is locally Noetherian. To check $f$ is locally of finite type, cover $X$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U$ by standard principal opens $D(g)\subseteq U$ of $\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the corresponding product chart has ring $A\otimes_k k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]_g\cong A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]_{g_A}$: the isomorphism sends $a\otimes t_j$ to $at_j$ and $1\otimes g^{-1}$ to $g_A^{-1}$, with inverse given by the same generators. This algebra is generated over $A$ by $t_1,\ldots,t_n,g_A^{-1}$, so these charts verify the locally-finite-type condition of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] once more to $f$ to conclude that $Y$ is locally Noetherian.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is flat. Indeed, over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the product with the whole affine space is $\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, by the tensor calculation in step 1. Its projection is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. The restriction to the open $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_kU$ has exactly the same source and target local rings at its points. Thus it is flat at each point by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. These opens cover $Y$, proving the assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof; hypotheses of Divisors Tag 0BD7 spelled out.

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, write $K=\kappa(x)$. The fibre $Y_x$ is $U_K=U\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$, an open of $\operatorname{Spec}K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$: the affine chart calculation of step 1 replaces $k[t]_g$ by $K[t]_{g_K}$ and the charts glue by their identical localization maps. The point $p\in U(k)$ base changes to a $K$-point, so this open is nonempty. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd], $K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ is a domain. Its spectrum is reduced and irreducible (the zero prime is generic); a nonempty open remains irreducible, and its local rings are the same domain localizations. It is therefore integral in the equivalent reduced/irreducible formulation of [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This checks integral nonempty fibres for every $x$, including the generic point.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof; hypotheses of Divisors Tag 0BD7 spelled out.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $X$ and put $K=\kappa(\eta)$. The tensor pullback $\mathcal N_\eta$ is invertible on $Y_\eta=U_K$: a local rank-one frame $e$ pulls back to the frame $1\otimes e$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-space-open-invertible-trivial] over the field $K$ to obtain $\mathcal N_\eta\simeq\mathcal O_{Y_\eta}$. Now [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback], applied to $f:Y\to X$ and $\mathcal N$, gives an invertible module $M$ on $X$ and $f^*M\simeq\mathcal N$: local Noetherianity and local finite type were proved in step 1, flatness in step 2, and integral nonempty fibres in step 3. The base $X$ is integral and normal by hypothesis. Thus all five hypotheses of that criterion, including generic-fibre triviality, have been checked.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof; hypotheses of Divisors Tag 0BD7 spelled out.

proof.text: For $r=p,q$, the map $i_r:X\to Y$ is the pair $(\operatorname{id}_X,r\circ(X\to\operatorname{Spec}k))$, so $f\circ i_r=\operatorname{id}_X$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pull back the isomorphism from step 4. The identity and composition isomorphisms in [def-pc-module-pullback] give $i_r^*\mathcal N\simeq i_r^*f^*M\simeq(f\circ i_r)^*M\simeq M$. Compose the isomorphism for $p$ with the inverse of the one for $q$ to obtain $i_p^*\mathcal N\simeq i_q^*\mathcal N$.
